clusters.title: The Open questions table holds rows that are not open: Q25 is decided and recorded in ADR 0008 yet stays, and the maintainer-settled rows (Q4, Q6, Q9, Q12, Q13, Q14, Q23) have no event that makes them due, against the table's own rule that a question leaves when it is settled.

clusters.change: Delete the Q25 row now; ADR 0008 is its record and 05 5.4 states the rule. In the paragraph above the table, replace 'A question leaves this table when it is settled' with 'A question leaves this table in the change that writes its ADR', and give the Settled by cell a grammar: 'probe ids, or maintainer, before the first release-candidate tag'. The plan task ids (T101, T005) leave the tables in the plan-task-id cluster; the duplicate interval row of L13-20 is in the interval cluster.

clusters.section: index: Open questions; index: Deferred decisions
clusters.title: Q9's 'Homebrew tap later' and Q23's 'a credential only if a private registry is needed' are deferrals written as open-question defaults, with no Deferred row and no event, while the index says a deferral without a row is an oversight.

clusters.change: Q9 Default: drop 'Homebrew tap later'. Q23 Default: drop the clause after 'cached by digest'. Add two Deferred rows: 'a Homebrew tap | GitHub releases only, verified as in J1 step 2 | the first issue asking for a tap; the decision says how the formula verifies provenance' and 'a host-settings credential for a private workload registry | descriptors are read anonymously (03 3.4) | the first workload in a private registry, written as an issue'. Add under each table heading one sentence restating ADR 0005's criterion: a question has a default the spec follows; a deferral is absent until its event.
clusters.cost: two cells shortened, two rows, two sentences
clusters.resolution_text: Apply for Q9 and Q23. The other half of L13b-22 (moving the token review interval and the ledger tuning rows to Open questions) is declined: the interval folds into the token row and the tuning row merges with rotation (see those clusters), which removes both rows instead of moving them.

clusters.title: The 'v1.1' bucket of 00 0.5 holds four items (the native egress queue in status, handoff --list filters, a Remote-SSH helper, a registry credential) with no trigger and no 'until then', beside a principle that says a deferral without a row is an oversight; Q23 lives in two tables.

clusters.change: Replace the v1.1 row of 00 0.5 and the parenthesis of 07 7.5 with Deferred rows: the native egress queue in status (until then: sbx's own command; reopened by the first native approval a user resolves without knowing it existed, written as an issue), handoff --list filters (until then: the full list; reopened by the first issue asking for one), a Remote-SSH helper (until then: none; reopened by the first issue asking for one), and the registry credential (merged with the Q23 row of the Q9/Q23 cluster). Change the 00 0.5 sentence 'anything that does not is marked v1.1' to 'anything that does not is a row of Deferred decisions'.
clusters.cost: one 00 0.5 row and sentence, one 07 7.5 parenthesis, three index rows
clusters.resolution_text: Recommend the rows above. The text change is small, but it removes the 'v1.1' label from 00 0.5, the scope justification, so the operator decides whether those four items stay promised for v1.1 or become plain deferrals.
clusters.operator_reason: changes the scope (00 0.5): the 'v1.1' label is a promise to a release, while a Deferred row promises nothing until its event

clusters.title: The kit publishing path is a deferral outside the Deferred table: six rows of design, including a host-settings key kits.source that 03 3.4 does not define, reopened by 'a maintainer decision', which ADR 0005 rule 3 does not accept as an event.
clusters.scenario: A reader of 06 6.6 writes kits.source into a settings file and the strict decoder of 03 3.4 refuses it; the Docker Hub limits written today will have changed when the trigger fires; promotion happens by no defined event.
clusters.change: Replace the table and the Docker Hub paragraph of 06 6.6 with the sentences today's design depends on (gate 2 records a content hash for a local kit; a published kit would be recorded by digest) and one Deferred row: 'publishing and signing product kits | local builds only, trusted as the release plus the config commits (06 6.1) | the first issue from a user who cannot build the local kits, or sbx accepting a signature for a local kit'. clusters.cost: one section shortened to a paragraph, one row, one citation

clusters.section: index: Deferred decisions (narrowing the sandbox's GitHub token)
clusters.title: The token-narrowing row, the acceptance of the widest decision in the project, has no producer for its triggers: 'every 2 autonomous work sessions' is counted by nothing (13 13.2 records no session start or end), and the security-log trigger depends on a log whose coverage the row itself calls unverified.
clusters.scenario: Six sessions pass and nobody counted; an agent merges and tags through the API and the security log of a personal account does not show it; the narrowing is never reconsidered while the operator's full reach stays with every sandbox.
clusters.change: Give the session trigger a producer that already exists: a session ends at its final handoff (08 8.3), so write the trigger as 'the second final handoff of the product project since the date of the last review, written in this row; romeu handoff --list shows them'. Each review rewrites that date. Take the security-log clause out of the trigger list and keep it as a sentence: 'the GitHub security log is not a trigger, its coverage being unverified (05 5.4)'.
clusters.cost: one cell rewritten; no new tool, the count is read from a list a command already prints
clusters.resolution_text: Recommend the handoff-count form above: it keeps the operator's cadence and replaces memory with a command's output. The alternative, a calendar date, needs an exception to ADR 0005 rule 3 recorded in ADR 0005.
clusters.operator_reason: the trigger is the operator's recorded decision in ADR 0008 and the risk it guards is accepted in 05 5.4; changing how it fires changes that decision record

clusters.section: index: Deferred decisions (the review interval of the token narrowing)
clusters.title: The row 'the review interval of the token narrowing' repeats the interval of the row above it and is reopened by 'the operator saying so', which no reader or check can see fire.
clusters.scenario: A reader updates the interval in one row and not the other; a reviewer cannot tell a fired trigger from an ignored one.
clusters.change: Delete the row and add to the token-narrowing row's trigger cell: 'The interval becomes every 10 sessions once the panel or a ledger view shows the agent's GitHub actions per session; that view existing is the event, and the operator then decides the change (ADR 0008).'
clusters.cost: one row deleted, one sentence added
clusters.resolution_text: Apply: what ADR 0008 decided (2 sessions, then 10 once review is cheap) stays; only the duplicate row and its unobservable trigger go. L0-12's other half (triggers no one observes) is answered by the issue-label cluster.

clusters.title: Many rows are reopened by events only a person notices ('The maintainer observes these', 'the first question about', 'written as an issue'), with no channel by which an adopter's event reaches anyone; no row names the check that detects its trigger, although ADR 0005 Consequences asks for it; and after round 8 no review round reads the table.
clusters.scenario: An adopter restores the ledger from a backup, a hash-chain trigger, and nobody upstream learns of it; tools/ci sequences passes because all three cells are filled; the step-table and dark-package triggers never fire because nothing compares them.
clusters.change: Add two sentences under the Deferred decisions heading: 'Where a check or a command output detects the event, the Reopened by cell names it. Any other event is reported, by whoever meets it, as an issue labelled deferred that names the row, and the table is read at each release-candidate tag.' Add the label to the CONTRIBUTING.md outline of 12 12.8. Rewrite the cells that say 'The maintainer observes these' or 'The maintainer observes it' as 'reported as an issue labelled deferred'. For the step-table row, name the check that detects drift: a test that the step names tools/ci all prints equal the rows of 10 10.2, whose landing also closes the row. For the dark-package row, name the check: a listing of packages no command reaches, read at each release-candidate tag.
clusters.cost: two sentences, one label, a few cells; no fourth column
clusters.resolution_text: Apply one issue label and one reading event instead of a 'Detected by' column: one channel for every human-observed trigger merges the per-row observers into one concept, and a release-candidate tag is an event, not a date.

clusters.section: index: Deferred decisions (finer visibility per project in the cross-project view)
clusters.title: The trigger 'the first private project on a machine that also runs a public one' cannot be observed: the spec has no notion of a private or public project (03 3.2), it misses projects of different clients that are all private, and the row names no observer.
clusters.scenario: A consultant runs client A and client B projects on one Mac; A's sandbox lists B's project name and activity times (13 13.6); the trigger never fires, because neither project is public.
clusters.change: Rewrite the trigger: 'projects whose repositories belong to more than one owner (a GitHub owner or a gitHosts entry) are synced on one machine, reported as an issue labelled deferred; or an issue asks that a project not be seen by the others'. Keep the until-then cell, which cites the accepted risk in 05 5.4.
clusters.cost: one cell
clusters.resolution_text: Apply the trigger rewrite only; a sync notice or a host-settings switch is the decision the trigger reopens. The accepted risk in 05 5.4 is unchanged.

clusters.title: The free-text note is reopened when an agent's need is 'written as an issue', but the agent, the only observer, is told nowhere that an issue is the channel, so the trigger cannot fire.

clusters.change: Rewrite the trigger as 'an issue labelled deferred asking for it', and add one sentence to the julieta skill's text: something no event id expresses goes into the handoff, and the agent opens an issue labelled deferred that names this row.
clusters.cost: one cell, one sentence in the skill
clusters.resolution_text: Apply without a CLI hint: the skill already carries the agent's instructions, and the label is the channel of the issue-label cluster.

clusters.section: index: Deferred decisions (docs versioning per release)
clusters.title: The docs-versioning row's 'until then' is itself a defect once v1.0.0 ships: a user on release N reads main's generated error ids, exit codes and command pages, and the trigger fires the first week with nothing reporting it.

clusters.resolution_text: Apply the link at the tag; attaching the docs as a release asset is a second mechanism for the same need and waits for the row's trigger.

clusters.title: Several Reopened by cells name plan steps (the start of T005, item e) instead of the event the step produces, while plan.md says the spec is the plan's source of truth.

clusters.resolution_text: Apply as proposed.
